rules.statement: Use se.sundsvall.dept44.problem.Problem for errors; never import org.zalando.problem.*
rules.rationale: Zalando Problem is not on the classpath in dept44 8+. Problem.valueOf(HttpStatus, detail) returns dept44 ThrowableProblem whose status is Spring HttpStatus.
rules.good_example: import se.sundsvall.dept44.problem.Problem; throw Problem.valueOf(NOT_FOUND, "errand %s not found".formatted(id));

rules.statement: Always use explicit imports — never wildcard imports
Static-import enums and constants — write NOT_FOUND, not HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND
Static-import AssertJ helpers (assertThat, tuple, …) — write assertThat(...) / tuple(...), never the full org.assertj.core.api.Assertions / org.assertj.core.groups.Tuple package path
rules.rationale: AssertJ's Assertions.assertThat is always static-imported. It only gets fully-qualified to dodge the name clash with Hamcrest's MatcherAssert.assertThat (used by the BeanMatchers testBean check). Resolve the clash the other way: static-import AssertJ (the frequently-used one, bare assertThat) and class-import Hamcrest (import org.hamcrest.MatcherAssert) so the single bean check reads MatcherAssert.assertThat — never the full org.hamcrest.MatcherAssert.assertThat package path.

rules.statement: Entity @Column(length) must match the column size in the Flyway migration
rules.rationale: If the JPA entity (and its @Size-validated API model) allow a longer string than the migration's varchar(N), a value that passes bean validation is truncated/rejected at insert (HTTP 500). The migration column and the entity @Column(length) must agree. Caught a real regression where errand_document.document_type was varchar(64) while the entity/@Size allowed 255.

rules.statement: No Lombok — write getters, setters, constructors, and builders explicitly
No ternary operator (?:) — use if/else, a helper method, or Optional
rules.rationale: Team standard: ternaries are banned outright in scit/dept44 Java.

rules.statement: Prefer Optional over null checks and ternaries for nullable handling
Variables and dependencies should be final whenever possible
Prefer method references over lambdas: .map(Mapper::toEntity), not .map(e -> toEntity(e))
Unused lambda parameters must be _ (Java 22+ unnamed variables): (root, _, cb) -> ...
Constructor injection with final dependencies — no @Autowired field/setter injection
rules.good_example:
private final FooService foo;
DemoService(FooService foo) { this.foo = foo; }

rules.statement: Throw Problem.valueOf(HttpStatus, detail) for errors; messages as constants with %s placeholders
rules.good_example:
private static final String ERRAND_NOT_FOUND = "errand %s not found";
throw Problem.valueOf(NOT_FOUND, ERRAND_NOT_FOUND.formatted(id));

rules.statement: Batch-lookup errors must name the missing subset, not report a generic 'none found'
No unused public methods — keep the service surface to what is actually called
Resources are thin: no business logic, delegate to the service layer
Resource classes are package-private (drop 'public')
REST controllers live in api/ and are named {Entity}Resource, not {Entity}Controller
API paths include the municipalityId path parameter: /{municipalityId}/...
rules.rationale: Municipality id 2281 is Sundsvall; never hardcode it.

rules.statement: No redundant @PathVariable name — rely on the parameter name (compiled with -parameters)
Each Resource needs two test classes: {Resource}Test (happy path) + {Resource}FailureTest (validation)
No enums in the API model layer — use String + @MemberOf(MyEnum.class) / @OneOf and @Schema(allowableValues=...)
API models: static create() factory, with*() fluent setters, manual equals/hashCode/toString; records for simple immutable DTOs
Annotate OffsetDateTime fields with @DateTimeFormat(iso = DATE_TIME)
POJO tests: testBean() (BeanMatchers/Hamcrest), testBuilderMethods(), testNoDirtOnCreatedBean()
Entity enum fields use @Enumerated(EnumType.STRING) — store as varchar, never ordinal int
String id with @UuidGenerator; @Column(name = snake_case) with explicit nullable/length
OffsetDateTime entity fields use @TimeZoneStorage(NORMALIZE)
Set column lengths in the entity (they flow into schema.sql); keep them consistent across like fields
All Feign clients and Spring Data repositories require @CircuitBreaker
@FeignClient(name = CLIENT_ID); Properties as a record with @ConfigurationProperties; error decoder + retry interceptor; request timeouts
Never log SSBTEK payloads or personnummer/income data — keep payload logging disabled
rules.rationale: Sensitive personal data; financial-aid already disables payload logging.

rules.statement: Mappers are static utility classes with a private constructor, null-safe via ofNullable()/emptyList()
rules.good_example: public final class DemoMapper { private DemoMapper() {} static DemoEntity toEntity(Demo d) { ... } }

rules.statement: Mapper method names: to{Target}, to{Target}Entity, to{Target}List, updateEntity
Schedulers use @Dept44Scheduled, not Spring's @Scheduled
Scheduler delegates to a {Job}Worker; reports health via Dept44HealthUtility; per-item error handling
AppTests extend AbstractAppTest with @WireMockAppTestSuite; fluent setupCall() chain; test method naming test01_, test02_
Use URL-safe invalid values in failure tests — never '#' (fragment delimiter truncates the path silently)
85% line + 85% branch coverage (JaCoCo) — builds fail below this
Keep openapi.yml in sync with the Resource; don't add endpoints without updating the spec; no enums leak into the generated model
Validate string-typed enum fields with @MemberOf/@OneOf; custom validators in api/validation with impls in api/validation/impl
Use .toList() instead of .collect(Collectors.toList()) (note it returns an immutable list); hoist constant expressions into static final fields
Prefer Spring's org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional over the Jakarta variant, used consistently across the service
Don't put Swagger/OpenAPI annotations on Feign client interfaces — they produce no docs; those belong on REST controllers
Don't declare entities Serializable without a reason; if Serializable is required, declare a serialVersionUID
Suffix JPA entity classes (and their tests) with 'Entity' to express purpose
JPA entities implement equals & hashCode (identity/business-key based) — BeanMatchers testBean expects them and collections/dedup rely on them
Use repository.deleteAll(entities) instead of entities.forEach(repo::delete) — one call, still per-entity through the persistence context so cascade = ALL fires and no blob is orphaned
Avoid List<List<X>> and other raw nested collections in models; wrap the inner list in a named type (e.g. FormSnapshotGroup) so the shape is workable and extensible
Use @Schema(requiredMode = REQUIRED) on mandatory fields (not the deprecated required=) with matching @NotBlank/@NotNull constraints
Name test classes with the singular 'Test' suffix (not 'Tests'), in camelCase methods without a redundant 'test_' prefix, and name the class after the class it actually exercises
